subject: Host Per-User Application Directories on a network environment

messages.author: 794570edb1de2b89
messages.subject: Host Per-User Application Directories on a network environment
parts: I am definitely not the server administrator but my company have a Shiny Server and it was setup using to host a directory of applications. The server administrators have to manage the directories for the users and to say the least is very complicated for the users and the server administrators. I suggested to change this to the users_dirs mode but was not able to successfully explain it. I have tested this in a simple environment where I have created local users (e.g., user1, user2) and I am able to host using the users_dir mode. However the server administrators have this on server where I am pretty sure the users do not exist locally. They exist in an active directory environment (LDAP). How can the shiny server be used in an LDAP environment. I saw the Shiny Server Pro have LDAP authentication but I dont think the issue is authentication. Any ideas/reference that will help me ask the right questions will help. Thanks

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Host Per-User Application Directories on a network environment
parts: Just a guess, usually these environments work by mirroring the LDAP user to the local server on-demand. So I'm guessing once you've logged in once, you'll have a /home/username directory and an entry in /etc/passwd.
